section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity Analogy
section_1.content: Begin by connecting the abstract derivative to a physical transformation. We move from measuring 'average speed' (change over a distance) to 'instantaneous speed' (the limit as the time interval vanishes).
section_1.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: Instead of saying the cheetah ran 60mph total, we zoom in on the exact micro-second it lunges to capture the velocity at that precise point.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Visual: The Secant-to-Tangent Transition
section_2.content: Recall the slope formula (rise/run). Visually demonstrate a secant line connecting two points on a curve, then animate the second point sliding along the curve toward the first until they merge into a single tangent line.
section_2.example: Visualize a roller coaster track; the 'secant' is a straight board connecting two peaks, while the 'tangent' is the exact tilt of the coaster car at a single point.

section_3.title: Core Concept: The Derivative as a Local Linear Transformer
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Transformational View': Instead of just a slope, define the derivative as a operator that transforms 'x' variations into 'y' variations. Zoom into a curve until it becomes a straight line; the derivative is the magnification factor of that local linear map.
section_3.example: Imagine a smartphone screen. As you zoom in on a small section of a curved map, the curved road looks like a perfectly straight path. The derivative tells you how much your vertical position shifts for every 1 unit of horizontal movement.

section_4.title: Visualizing Sensitivity: The 'What-If' Machine
section_4.content: Reframe the derivative (f'(x)) as a sensitivity gauge. If I nudge 'x' by a tiny amount, how much does the output 'f(x)' amplify or shrink that nudge? The derivative is the scaling factor of the input change.
section_4.example: A smart thermostat: If the derivative of temperature relative to power is 2, a 1% increase in power leads to a 2% change in heat output. The derivative is the 'knob' turning efficiency.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
section_5.content: Conclude that the derivative is not just a calculation, but a 'zoom-in' tool that reveals the linear truth hidden within complex curves. It turns dynamic change into a static, manageable ratio.
section_5.example: Final shot: A complex, swirling animation of a wave smoothing out into a single, perfectly straight arrow indicating direction and rate of change.
